info.name: Home Based Care API
info.description:
Home Based Care (HBC) service, NURSE / PHYSIO / CARETAKER bookings.

Identity: users, login and tokens live in the separate auth service. Every request sends
Authorization: Bearer <access token>; HBC takes the user id from the token `sub` and the role from its
`role` claim (verified against the auth service JWKS when AUTH_JWKS_URL is set).

Against a deployed server: in the environment set baseUrl and four access tokens from the auth service:
adminToken (SUPER_ADMIN), providerToken and rivalToken (two different HBC accounts), patientToken (PATIENT).
Against a local server without AUTH_JWKS_URL, leave them empty: the collection generates unsigned dev tokens
with fresh user ids for every run.

Payment: with PAYMENT_PROVIDER=mock the booking is PAID at once. With the real payment-service the pay step
returns a Razorpay checkoutUrl and stops the run: pay with a test card, then run the rest of
"4. Booking flow" from "Patient - payment status".

Roles: SUPER_ADMIN, PATIENT and HBC (every care provider). A provider picks their care type
(NURSE, PHYSIO or CARETAKER) when registering their profile; it is fixed after that.
HBC stores only service-provider profiles. Patient contact details are sent with each booking.
There is no admin verification: providers can pick bookings as soon as they register.
Matching: same care type, and the booking is in the provider's pincode or within SERVICE_RADIUS_KM
(default 10 km) of the provider's latitude/longitude.

Folders run top to bottom as one end-to-end flow (collection variables carry ids between steps).
Change careType to PHYSIO or CARETAKER to register the providers and run the same flow for another care type.

item.description: Providers (X-Role: HBC) register their profile under their gateway X-User-Id with a care type (NURSE, PHYSIO or CARETAKER), pincode, latitude and longitude. No verification step.

item.name: 8. Payment webhook
item.description:
POST /api/v1/hbc/payments/webhook is called by payment-service (PAID / FAILED), not by apps. It has no bearer
token: it is authenticated by X-Payment-Timestamp + X-Payment-Signature =
hex(HMAC-SHA256(PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET, timestamp + "." + rawBody)).

These requests only use a booking id that does not exist, so they never change any data.
Set webhookSecret in the environment (= the server PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET) to also check that the secret matches.

exec: pm.collectionVariables.set('webhookBookingId', pm.variables.replaceIn('{{$guid}}')); // a booking that does not exist

variable.description: Host only, e.g. http://localhost:4000 or the gateway URL. Paths carry /api/v1/hbc.

exec: // Tokens: set adminToken / providerToken / rivalToken / patientToken in the ENVIRONMENT (access tokens
// from authservice: SUPER_ADMIN, two HBC providers, PATIENT). Environment values win over the collection ones.
// Without them (local server, no AUTH_JWKS_URL) unsigned dev tokens with fresh ids are generated per run;
// a server with AUTH_JWKS_URL (production) rejects those.
const devToken = (role, exp) => b64({ alg: 'none', typ: 'JWT' }) + '.' +
b64({ sub: pm.variables.replaceIn('{{$guid}}'), role, exp: exp || Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 3600 }) + '.dev';
// The user ids the tests compare against are the tokens' `sub`.
const sub = (t) => { try { return JSON.parse(atob(t.split('.')[1].replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/'))).sub; } catch (e) { return ''; } };
